summary: A SIGKILL'd dispatch leaves TWO stale locks, not one. The second (the per-cwd dispatch lock, TTL = runner timeoutMs) is undisclosed, and attempting recovery while it is still held permanently links a synthetic status:"failed" RunResult to the Assignment, flipping the actor from `late` to `failed` with no CLI retry door. tsk-47l's own documented repro/workaround triggers this worse bug when followed promptly. In this repo's real config the hazard window is 35 minutes, not the 60s the proof sandbox happened to use.
location: src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs:467-483; src/runner/coordination/session-engine.mjs:377-400; src/runner/main-checkout-lock.mjs:77; bin/fgos.mjs:4565 (unlock), 3118/3190 (coordination sub-verbs); src/verbs/coordination/schema.mjs:569-574; proofs/P05.1/doer-report.md Area 6 steps 5-6; proofs/P05.1/crash-state-snapshot.md sections 4-5; tsk-47l
evidence: Independently reproduced end to end in an isolated sandbox. (1) Killed a real `fgos coordination run` PID 3895508 mid-dispatch with SIGKILL; ESRCH probe and `ps -p` both confirm dead; exec-slow-started.marker present, exec-slow-finished.marker absent. On-disk state identical to the Doer's: assignment.json + dispatch.claim + runs/01/{run.json,dispatch-plan.json}, run.json frozen at "status": "running", no result.json. (2) `rm dispatch.claim` then re-ran the identical operation 58s after the kill: exit=1. runs/02/result.json was written with "status": "failed" and agentClaim.summary 'dispatch for cwd "..." is already in flight (held for 58s)'. That error originates at src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs:480, from a SECOND lock: `acquireMainCheckoutLock(fgosDir, { ttlMs: timeoutMs, releaseOnExit: true, lockFile: dispatchLockFile(cwd) })` at cli.mjs:467-474. SIGKILL prevents releaseOnExit from ever firing, so the lock survives until its TTL lapses. (3) The engine LINKED that failed run: event `{"type":"result-linked","payload":{"assignmentId":"asgn_aap_driver_op_008","runId":"run_asgn_aap_driver_op_008_02"}}`. `fgos coordination show` then reports the synthesizer under quorum.failed, no longer `late`. (4) A third resume at 108s (TTL long lapsed) still exits 1 and creates NO runs/03 -- it short-circuits at the priorLink check (session-engine.mjs:377-381) and returns the failed result as resumed:true, forever. (5) No CLI door recovers it: `fgos unlock` (bin/fgos.mjs:4565) calls acquireMainCheckoutLock WITHOUT the lockFile option, so it targets the default main-checkout lock, never dispatchLockFile(cwd); `retrySessionTask` (session-engine.mjs:4381) is unreachable because the request schema accepts only operation/authorize/contribution/human-turn (schema.mjs:569-574) and coordination exposes only run/show/launch-master-loop/chain (bin/fgos.mjs:3190). (6) A workaround DOES exist and I verified it: a fresh `authorize` with a new authorizationId/invocationKey creates a NEW Assignment (asgn_aap_driver_op_009), dispatches cleanly, and quorum recovers to failed:[] with the synthesizer completed. But it consumes one invocation, so for the two bindings that declare activation.maxInvocations: 2 (`revise-synthesis` and `revise-explanation`, core/coordination-protocols/architecture-advisory-panel-v1.yaml:513-523) a crash during the second invocation is genuinely unrecoverable through CLI doors. (7) Severity is driven by window width: the proof sandbox used runner.timeoutMs 60000, which is why the Doer -- who let more than 60s elapse between the kill and the resume -- never saw it. This repo's own .fgos/config.json sets runner.timeoutMs 2100000 (35 minutes). tsk-47l's verify field instructs the fixer to 'confirm process dead, then re-run the identical operation step through the CLI', i.e. promptly, which inside a 35-minute window lands squarely in the poisoning path.
recommendation: Do not close P05.1's Area 6 on the current characterization. Extend tsk-47l (or file a sibling) to cover all three facts: (a) the per-cwd dispatch lock is a second SIGKILL-surviving lock with no CLI door and a TTL equal to runner.timeoutMs; (b) a DispatchError raised while that lock is held is currently persisted AND linked as a real failed RunResult -- a transient infrastructure refusal should not become the Assignment's durable outcome, so `dispatch-in-flight` should fail the call without writing/linking a result; (c) `retrySessionTask` already exists as the engine's retry primitive but no CLI door exposes it, which is the common root cause of both the stale-claim gap and this one. Also add a warning to tsk-47l's verify recipe that re-running promptly is currently destructive. Separately, note in the recovery documentation that SIGKILL of the CLI does NOT kill the executor: the executor is spawned detached as its own process-group leader, and I confirmed orphans 3895521/3895530 still alive after the parent kill -- any future auto-reconciliation must probe the executor's process group, not just the CLI PID, or it will re-introduce the exact double-dispatch race dispatch.claim exists to prevent.

summary: crash-state-snapshot.md opens by asserting its contents are 'copied verbatim from the real terminal session ... not reconstructed afterward', but section 1's dead-process confirmation shows output that no `ps` invocation can produce. The underlying fact is true and independently reproducible; the transcript is synthesized.
evidence: The file presents three blocks of the form `$ ps -p 3730502 -o pid,stat,cmd` followed by a `    PID STAT CMD` header and a line `3730502_GONE_CONFIRMED`. I ran the real command against that same now-dead PID: `ps -p 3730502 -o pid,stat,cmd` prints ONLY the header line `    PID STAT CMD` and exits 1; with headers suppressed (`-o pid=,stat=,cmd=`) it prints nothing at all and exits 1. The string `<pid>_GONE_CONFIRMED` is a marker the Doer's own shell produced (almost certainly via a `|| echo "${PID}_GONE_CONFIRMED"` fallback), not ps output. My own independent crash run logged the honest form: `ps -p 3895508 raw output: ""  (empty string == genuinely gone)`. The substance of the claim holds -- I confirmed dead processes by the same two independent mechanisms (ESRCH probe plus ps) -- so this is a presentation-integrity defect, not a false conclusion.
recommendation: Correct section 1 to show either the real command output or the actual composite command that generated the marker, and drop or narrow the blanket 'verbatim, not reconstructed' claim at the top of the file. In a cell whose entire product is evidence fidelity, a synthesized line inside a block labelled verbatim undermines the credibility of the artifacts that ARE genuine -- and most of this evidence set is genuine.

summary: The stderr `provider=` field that Area 4 relies on as committed evidence does not always match the authoritative RunResult provenance: for default-executor dispatches stderr prints provider=node while the RunResult records provider "claude".
evidence: out-01-framing-shaping.stderr.log line 1 reads `executor=node via=cli-spawn provider=node model=test-model tier=critical`. In my clean re-run of the identical request the corresponding RunResult (asgn_aap_driver_op_001/runs/01/result.json) records provenance provider {"value":"claude","source":{"scope":"registeredExecutor","id":"node"}} with model source runnerConfig id "claude.critical". The two disagree on the provider field. For the two roles Area 4 actually claims (exec-family-a/family-a and exec-family-b/family-b) stderr and RunResult agree exactly, so Area 4's conclusion is unaffected.
recommendation: Worth knowing only because finding P051-R-03 leaves the stderr log as Area 4's sole committed artifact. Once the real result.json files are committed this stops mattering for this cell. If the divergence is unintended it belongs in its own item against the dispatch log line, not this track.

summary: grantedContextRefs are accepted without being validated against existing Assignments, so the audit record of what context a reveal granted can carry dangling references.
evidence: In my sandbox the visibility session's real assignments were asgn_aap_driver_op_005/006/007, yet req-attack-visibility-03 authorized successfully (exit 0, appended true, operation-authorized event auth_critique_late written) while declaring grantedContextRefs ["asgn_aap_driver_op_016", "asgn_aap_driver_op_017", "$ref:shapeConstraint"] -- op_016 and op_017 do not exist in that store. The premature-reveal refusal in req-attack-visibility-02 likewise fired on the visibility window before any context-ref check, with the same non-existent refs. This does NOT weaken Area 2's claim: the gate keys off real quorum completion of the shaper trio, which I verified independently in both directions.
recommendation: No action required for P05.1's own claims. Flag it for P05.2 so the published example requests do not normalize dangling grantedContextRefs, and consider whether the authorize step should reject refs that name no Assignment in the session -- the field exists to make a reveal auditable, and an unvalidated one is weaker than it looks.

summary: Only 3 of the main chain's 14 dispatched operations were routed through a declared per-role binding; the other 11 fell back to the global default executor because 8 of the 11 main-chain requests omit actors[]. Benign in this sandbox, but the report presents Area 4 without noting how narrow the confined slice is.
location: proofs/P05.1/requests/req-02, req-07, req-08, req-09, req-10, req-12 (all dispatch operations with no actors[]); proofs/P05.1/doer-report.md Area 4
evidence: Tabulating every request: only req-01 (2 of its 5 operations), req-04 and req-06 declare actors[]. req-02 (2 ops), req-07, req-08, req-09, req-10 and req-12 (1 op each) declare none. run.mjs's findActor reads the CURRENT request only and never the session manifest, so those calls resolve through the global default -- visible in out-01-framing-shaping.stderr.log as the `executor=node ... provider=node` lines interleaved with the family-a/family-b ones. Harmless here because the proof config's default executor is itself a local fake (`node exec-family-a.mjs`).
recommendation: Add one sentence to the Area 4 write-up stating that the heterogeneous claim covers the 3 explicitly-bound dispatches and that the remainder ran on the default binding. This matters for P05.2, which runs against real providers on real projects: an unrepeated actors[] there silently routes later calls to the unconfined default executor rather than the roster the panel was opened with.
